svg.aria-label: How an Actio run moves in swarm v2: the stages left to right with the five checks in parallel, the loop inside every agent, the four lanes, and the measured change.
svg.title: How an Actio run moves
svg.desc: How a run moves. Stage 1: bug-historian writes the regression brief by script (bugs.mjs brief), then tech-architect writes the ADR and task briefs and owns the design-authority gate. Stage 2, in parallel: backend-engineer, whose database track goes straight to review, and ux-designer. Stage 3, in parallel: ux-auditor owns the design gate and ux-writer owns the copy gate, writing from the string slots without waiting for the design gate. Stage 4: frontend-engineer. Stage 5, five in parallel: peer-reviewer (review-1of3), code-analyst (review-2of3), code-steward (review-3of3), security-analyst (security) and the bug-historian regression guard by script (bugs.mjs guard, regression-guard). When all five pass: stage 6 engineering-lead (engineering) runs verify.mjs once, and the bundle is reused by qc-engineer (stage 7), qc-lead (stage 8, quality) and release-engineer (stage 9, release) for the same tree key. Stage 10: bug-historian records new BUGS.md entries. Close: the orchestrator runs run.mjs close and owns run-closure. Between every stage the orchestrator makes at most four tool calls: run.mjs next, run.mjs dispatch, every due agent in one message, run.mjs next. A hook writes every dispatch and return to the ledger. Inside every agent: dispatch, checkpoint (handoff.json with status working and a plan with Risk lines), execute, self-check with evidence, validated handoff (run.mjs handoff), and a return of at most 8 lines. A resumed agent starts from the checkpoint. Lanes: micro for docs, agents, skills or config; standard-ui for the UI track only; standard-db for the database track only; full for both tracks or anything touching privacy, RLS, grants, auth, the state machine or evidence closure. Measured over 7 runs: 804M tokens and 52.5 of 75.5 hours locked out by spend limits. Preload per agent was 49 to 262 KB and is capped at 45 KB. Per pass, plan.md and review.md (medians 14 KB and 10 KB) give way to fields in one handoff.json.
svg.text: Swarm v2. Scripts do the bookkeeping, agents do the judgement, and every gate keeps its one owner.
A stage starts when its upstream gates pass. Boxes stacked in one column run in parallel. A fix is re-checked as a diff, not a full re-review.
the database track goes straight to review

g.text: between every stage, at most four tool calls
one prompt per due stage, brief slice inlined
every due agent in one message
on return; a handoff is read only to reject or escalate
A hook writes every dispatch and return to the ledger.

svg.text: same tree key: the bundle is reused, never rebuilt
The five steps stay and the paperwork goes. Plan, checks and findings live in handoff.json. No plan.md, no review.md.

g.text: or fix and run it again

svg.text: The orchestrator picks the lane from the files the change will touch and records why. Shehab can override.

g.text: Docs, agents, skills or config only.
No product code and no scripts.
One product track: the UI only.
One product track: the database only.
Both tracks, or privacy, RLS, grants,
auth, the state machine or closure.
